statusDetail: Coverage complete across 58 catalog checks and four representative paths. Authentication systems on separate origins were not covered.

page.framework: Server-rendered HTML with Bootstrap/jQuery; separate legacy fixed-width and current-account templates.
page.notes: Coverage includes the public gateway, corporate landing, FAQ content template, and current-account start journey. External YONO login, authenticated banking, payment completion, and destructive account actions were excluded because they cross origin and require credentials.

paths.description: Public gateway homepage, representative of navigation and the personal/corporate login entry points.
Legacy corporate banking homepage, representative of the older fixed-width corporate template.
Corporate FAQ listing, representative of content/disclosure pages and the legacy mobile/reflow behavior.
Current-account application landing and Start New Application journey, representative of the primary transactional flow.

findings.summary: The gateway ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, and computed styles report color-scheme: normal with white surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: The scrolling announcement keeps animating when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but still found a running 60,000 ms marquee animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable the marquee animation under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and expose the announcement as static text.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes use abrupt swaps rather than view transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules, while the representative site uses cross-document navigation and accordion/state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route and disclosure changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome is static and does not respond to scroll position.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots and CSS inspection show fixed/static navigation with no scroll-state container rules or progress cue on long pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained sticky header or scroll-position cue where it helps users retain context.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays rely on legacy Bootstrap/manual positioning rather than resilient anchored placement.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found Bootstrap menu/dialog structures and no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native popover plus CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions for transient menus and tooltips.

findings.summary: Stacked notices and a moving announcement dominate the gateway before core content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains two full-width warning banners plus a continuously moving announcement before the personal-banking action.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate urgent messaging into one concise, static, dismissible notice and preserve the primary task hierarchy.

findings.summary: Transient UI is implemented with custom Bootstrap div dialogs and JavaScript links.
findings.evidence: The accessibility probe found six div-based role=dialog modals and 18 javascript: links rather than native dialog/popover/details controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace custom modal/disclosure wiring with dialog, popover, details, and real buttons or links as appropriate.

findings.summary: Dense legacy chrome competes with core banking actions.
findings.evidence: The corporate template screenshot shows a dense tab bar, banner, announcement panels, decorative imagery, and compact 12 px text around the primary login action.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce decorative framing and repeated navigation, enlarge core content, and establish a clearer action hierarchy.

findings.summary: Representative pages do not reliably reflow on mobile.
findings.evidence: The gateway overflows by 33 px at 360 px. The FAQ lacks a viewport meta tag and renders a 980 px desktop canvas scaled to fit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid viewport declaration to every template, remove fixed 980 px wrappers, and use fluid intrinsic layouts.

findings.summary: Components depend on fixed widths and viewport-era styling rather than adapting to their containers.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero container rules; the corporate template includes fixed widths such as #wrapper { width: 980px } and many fixed-size panels.
findings.suggestedFix: Refactor reusable cards, navigation, and content regions with intrinsic sizing and container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target support are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the navigation toggle with outline:none and counted 23 controls below 24 px in at least one dimension; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge or space interactive targets to at least the recommended minimum.

findings.summary: The current-account application journey dead-ends immediately.
findings.evidence: Following Start New Application leads directly to “Your session has expired” instead of the registration form, before any user input.
findings.suggestedFix: Start a fresh application session on entry, preserve it through the flow, and test the journey end to end without stale-session state.

findings.summary: The gateway’s main content paints too slowly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP/FCP at 4.4 s; the raw-CDP trace measured LCP/FCP at 8.23 s under the observed run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP, remove render blockers, compress delivery, and defer noncritical carousel assets.

findings.summary: The FAQ template has a material load-time layout shift.
findings.evidence: The 360 px FAQ layout run recorded CLS 0.139, including a 0.137 shift around 6.1 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content and imagery and remove moving/late layout changes from the FAQ template.

findings.summary: Render-blocking, uncompressed, poorly cached resources delay the page.
findings.evidence: HAR/Lighthouse found four VeryHigh-priority blocking stylesheets, four synchronous head scripts, uncompressed HTML/CSS/JS, weak cache lifetimes, and an estimated 3.27 s render-blocking saving.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress text, set durable immutable caching for versioned assets, inline only critical CSS, and defer noncritical scripts/styles.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 264 KiB unused CSS and 96 KiB unused JavaScript, alongside unminified CSS/JS opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused Bootstrap/plugin code per template, split bundles by feature, and minify production assets.

findings.summary: Some links lack reliable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and label-content-name-mismatch; the image audit also found one image without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a programmatic name matching its visible label and meaningful images accurate alt text.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and semantic structure are inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: The gateway toggle computes outline:none when focused, while the legacy corporate pages omit a main landmark and even a visible h1 in the inspected DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Use consistent landmarks and heading hierarchy, and add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator to every control.

findings.summary: Legacy pages use cramped, fixed 12 px typography and scaled desktop layouts.
findings.evidence: Computed styles show 12 px Tahoma throughout the fixed 980 px corporate template; on mobile the whole FAQ canvas is scaled down rather than reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use fluid, user-scalable type with comfortable line height and responsive measures instead of shrinking a desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow and target sizing fail on representative pages.
findings.evidence: The FAQ has no viewport meta and exposes a 980 px layout at a 360 px condition; Lighthouse failed touch-target sizing.
findings.suggestedFix: Make every template reflow at narrow/zoomed widths and enlarge controls without disabling user zoom.

findings.summary: The gateway logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit failed for the tested navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the logged network/runtime errors and add production monitoring for uncaught exceptions.

findings.summary: Image and document assets are not consistently soundly authored.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 23 of 24 images without explicit dimensions, 23 legacy-format images, and one oversized image; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height, preserve aspect ratio, and serve responsive modern-format sources.

findings.summary: DevTools reports platform hygiene issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the inspector-issues audit; the DOM also contains 18 javascript: pseudo-links that bypass native link/button behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Clear DevTools Issues and replace javascript: URLs with semantic buttons or crawlable href links.

findings.summary: Important navigation is not fully crawlable or consistently mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found 18 javascript: links, Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors, and the FAQ template lacks viewport metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and add correct viewport metadata to all public templates.

findings.summary: Canonical, robots, and sitemap indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: No canonical URL was present; /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both returned branded 404 rejection pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid robots.txt and sitemap, add self-referencing canonicals where appropriate, and keep indexing policy consistent.

findings.summary: The public bank gateway lacks structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags on the organization/service gateway.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching the visible page.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but key security headers and cookie posture are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no HSTS or nosniff and a CSP allowing unsafe-inline; all four observed cookies use SameSite=None, with one not HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS and nosniff, tighten CSP away from unsafe-inline, and use the strictest viable SameSite/HttpOnly cookie settings.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: No frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy was observed, and the CSP lacks the documented clickjacking defense.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (and compatible X-Frame-Options), strict Referrer-Policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and evaluate Trusted Types for sensitive flows.

findings.summary: The account flow starts in stale runtime state.
findings.evidence: A fresh navigation to Start New Application immediately rendered a session-expired state, showing that initial session state is not stabilized.
findings.suggestedFix: Create/refresh session state atomically before rendering the application route and preserve user context across navigation.

findings.summary: Missing infrastructure routes return a dead-end rejection page.
findings.evidence: Both robots.txt and sitemap.xml returned 404 pages saying the URL was rejected and offered only a support ID, with no recovery navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correct machine-readable routes and provide useful recovery/navigation on human-facing HTTP error pages.

findings.summary: Language and bidirectional layout foundations are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The multilingual current-account pages have an empty html lang attribute, and legacy CSS uses extensive physical left/right properties and fixed positioning.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the correct lang/dir per locale and migrate layout rules to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: The account-opening flow is not dependable or continuous.
findings.evidence: The advertised Start New Application action immediately reports an expired session on a fresh visit, preventing account setup.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair session initiation and add end-to-end checks for start, resume, expiry recovery, confirmation, and safe reauthentication.

findings.summary: The gateway transfers a large set of unoptimized carousel images.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 5.44 MB, of which 4.84 MB was images; 23 images use legacy JPG/PNG, 23 lack dimensions, and responsive srcset is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert banners to AVIF/WebP, generate responsive srcset/sizes, set dimensions, and fetch only the active/nearby slide.

findings.summary: Hidden carousel media is eagerly downloaded without immediate user value.
findings.evidence: The network run downloaded 32 images and multiple 1,140–1,920 px banners, including many hidden slides, during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load nonvisible slides, cap prefetching to the next slide, and deprioritize decorative/background work.

findings.summary: The media budget is disproportionate to the simple gateway task.
findings.evidence: Although known trackers were absent, first-party images alone transferred 4.84 MB for a page whose core task is choosing a login or service link.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a media/page-weight budget, defer nonessential banners, and cache optimized variants durably.

taskList.title: Repair fresh-session initialization and verify the current-account journey end to end.
Replace fixed-width legacy templates with fluid, reflowing layouts and consistent viewport metadata.
Cut the initial image payload and render-blocking chain, with responsive modern images, compression, caching, and deferred scripts.
Restore accessible names, semantic landmarks, visible focus, and adequately sized controls.
Harden response headers, CSP, cookie attributes, clickjacking defenses, referrer policy, and permissions policy.
Publish valid crawlable links, robots.txt, sitemap, canonical URLs, and structured/social metadata.
Consolidate page notices and migrate custom modal/menu controls to native semantic primitives.
Honor dark mode and reduced-motion preferences while preserving contrast.
Reserve late content space and remove the FAQ layout shift.
Set correct language metadata and replace physical left/right CSS with logical properties.
Resolve console and DevTools issues and replace javascript pseudo-links with native controls.
Add restrained state and route transition cues where they improve orientation.
Serve useful recovery for HTTP failures and machine-readable infrastructure routes.
